description: Experience the sublime richness of Butter Chicken, a beloved Indian classic known for its creamy tomato-based gravy and tender chicken. This Murgh Makhani recipe brings the authentic flavors of Delhi right to your kitchen, offering a truly comforting and aromatic meal. Indulge in its velvety texture and perfectly balanced sweet and savory notes.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, garam masala, lemon juice, and salt. Mix well to coat all chicken pieces. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours for deeper flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, without overcrowding the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until the chicken is lightly browned and cooked through. Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, melt another 1 tablespoon of butter. Add chopped onions and sauté until translucent, about 3-4 minutes. Stir in the remaining ginger-garlic paste, green cardamom, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Build the Gravy Flavor
instructions.text: Add tomato puree, turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, and a pinch of salt. Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mixture thickens and the oil separates from the sides. Drain the soaked cashews and add them to the pan. Cook for another 2 minutes.

instructions.title: Blend and Simmer
instructions.text: Remove the bay leaf, cardamom pods, and cinnamon stick from the gravy base (if desired, for a smoother texture). Transfer the mixture to a blender and blend until completely smooth. You may need to add a splash of water if it is too thick. Pour the blended gravy back into the pan.

instructions.title: Combine Chicken and Finish
instructions.text: Add the cooked chicken pieces to the smooth gravy. Stir in the sugar and bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Stir in the heavy cream and the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter. Crush the dried fenugreek leaves between your palms and add to the curry. Simmer for 2 more minutes, but do not boil after adding cream.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve your authentic Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani hot with naan, roti, or basmati rice for a truly delightful Indian lunch.

tips: For an extra smoky flavor, grill or char the marinated chicken in an oven or air fryer before adding to the gravy.
Soaking cashews is crucial for a smooth, rich gravy without a grainy texture. You can also add a tablespoon of almond meal for extra thickness and creaminess.
Always add cream and dried fenugreek leaves (Kasuri Methi) at the very end of cooking and do not boil the curry afterward to prevent curdling and preserve the delicate flavors.
article:
Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani: Your Ultimate Guide to a Beloved Indian Lunch

Imagine a dish so rich, so creamy, and so utterly comforting that it transports you to the bustling streets of Delhi with every bite. That, my friends, is Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, a culinary masterpiece that has captured hearts worldwide. Perfect for a hearty lunch, this iconic Indian recipe offers a symphony of flavors – tender chicken swimming in a velvety tomato-based gravy, subtly spiced and finished with a generous swirl of butter and cream. If you've ever dreamt of recreating that restaurant-quality taste in your own kitchen, you've come to the right place. Get ready to embark on a delicious journey to master one of India's most cherished dishes.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

Butter Chicken, known in Hindi as Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter." Originating in Delhi in the 1950s, this dish was a brilliant innovation by Kundan Lal Gujral, the founder of Moti Mahal restaurant. The story goes that he needed a way to use leftover tandoori chicken, and so he simmered it in a rich tomato gravy, creating a sensation. The key to its irresistible appeal lies in the delicate balance of sweet, tangy, and savory notes, achieved through a blend of pureed tomatoes, aromatic spices like garam masala, cumin, and fenugreek (kasoori methi), and the luxurious touch of butter and cream. Unlike spicier curries, Butter Chicken offers a milder, more approachable flavor profile, making it a universal favorite and an excellent introduction to Indian cuisine. Its vibrant orange hue and smooth texture are as inviting as its taste, making it an ideal choice for a satisfying lunch.

## Ingredients You Need

To create the magic of Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani, gather these fresh and flavorful ingredients:

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain full-fat yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1/2 teaspoon garam masala
*   Salt to taste

For the Makhani Gravy:
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon cumin powder
*   1 teaspoon coriander powder
*   1/2 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1/4 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1/2 cup tomato paste or 2 large fresh tomatoes, pureed
*   1/4 cup cashews, soaked in hot water for 15 minutes
*   1/2 cup water or chicken broth
*   1/2 teaspoon sugar (optional, to balance tanginess)
*   1/2 teaspoon kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1/2 cup heavy cream
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these steps to craft your perfect Butter Chicken:

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring each piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, for maximum flavor.

2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in batches, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until lightly browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove the cooked chicken and set aside.

3.  **Prepare the Gravy Base:** In the same pan, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

4.  **Add Spices and Tomatoes:** Reduce heat to low. Add cumin powder, coriander powder, red chili powder, and turmeric powder. Sauté for 30 seconds, stirring constantly to prevent burning. Immediately add the tomato paste (or pureed tomatoes) and cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mixture thickens and the oil starts to separate from the sides.

5.  **Blend the Gravy:** Add the soaked cashews and water (or broth) to the tomato mixture. Bring to a simmer, then remove from heat. Carefully transfer the mixture to a blender (or use an immersion blender) and blend until completely smooth. Pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for an extra silky texture – this step is crucial for authentic Murgh Makhani.

6.  **Combine and Finish:** Return the pan with the sieved gravy to low heat. Stir in the cooked chicken. Add sugar (if using), crushed kasoori methi, and salt to taste. Simmer for 5-10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to absorb the rich gravy.

7.  **Add Cream and Garnish:** Just before serving, stir in the heavy cream. Heat gently for a minute or two, but do not boil after adding the cream, as it can curdle. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

*   **Marination is Key:** The longer you marinate the chicken, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight marination is highly recommended for the best Butter Chicken.
*   **Achieve Silky Smoothness:** Don't skip blending the gravy thoroughly and passing it through a sieve. This step ensures the signature smooth, luxurious texture of Murgh Makhani.
*   **Kasoori Methi Magic:** Dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) are non-negotiable. Crush them between your palms before adding to release their unique, slightly bitter, and aromatic flavor that is characteristic of Butter Chicken.
*   **Balance Your Flavors:** Taste and adjust! The beauty of this dish is its balance. Add a pinch more sugar if your tomatoes are too tangy, or a little more salt/chili powder if it needs a kick. A final swirl of butter before serving adds extra richness.
*   **The "Dhungar" Technique (Optional):** For an authentic smoky flavor, heat a small piece of charcoal until red hot. Place it in a small steel bowl in the center of the finished curry. Drizzle a teaspoon of ghee or oil over the charcoal, cover the pot immediately, and let it smoke for 5-7 minutes. Remove charcoal before serving.

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with a variety of accompaniments. For a classic Indian lunch experience, serve it piping hot with fluffy basmati rice, warm garlic naan bread, or soft roti. The bread is perfect for scooping up every last drop of that incredible gravy. A simple side salad of sliced cucumbers, onions, and tomatoes, perhaps with a squeeze of lemon, can offer a refreshing contrast to the richness of the curry. You can also serve it with a dollop of fresh yogurt or raita to further cool and balance the palate.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is divine, there are many ways to adapt it to your taste and dietary needs:

*   **Vegetarian Murgh Makhani:** For a delicious meat-free version, substitute chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese), tofu, or even chickpeas. Simply pan-fry or bake the paneer/tofu until golden before adding it to the gravy.
*   **Spice Level:** If you prefer more heat, increase the amount of red chili powder or add a finely chopped green chili to the gravy. For a milder version, reduce the chili powder or use sweet paprika for color.
*   **Healthier Twist:** To reduce calories, use boneless, skinless chicken breast and opt for low-fat yogurt and milk instead of heavy cream. You can also reduce the amount of butter. The flavor will be slightly different but still delicious.
*   **Smoky Flavor without Charcoal:** If you don't have charcoal, you can achieve a subtle smoky flavor by grilling or broiling your marinated chicken until it gets some char marks before adding it to the gravy.
*   **Nut-Free Option:** If you have a nut allergy, you can substitute cashews with sunflower seeds or skip them entirely. The gravy might be slightly less thick, but still flavorful.
*   **Tomato Variations:** While fresh tomatoes are great, canned crushed tomatoes or tomato puree work perfectly well, especially when fresh ones aren't in season.

This journey to create your own Murgh Makhani is more than just cooking; it's an exploration of rich flavors and a testament to the comforting power of Indian cuisine. Whether it's for a special occasion or a simple, satisfying lunch, this Butter Chicken recipe is sure to become a cherished favorite in your culinary repertoire. Enjoy every creamy, delicious bite!
